status: APPROVED: the engineer approved this look per graphics preset on 2026-10-13 (art PR #148, issue #140) as the game's recommended look: Low = ladder variant 3 (AgX, sky, eye catch light), Medium = 4 (+SSAO), High = 5 (+soft shadows), Ultra = 6 (+SSS on the clay), all at tonemap exposure 0.9. Still open: the hair 5 to 7 L* darker than Blender's, and the game-side wiring is untested. Amended 2026-10-19 (art #196, comment 6272668389): the characters' lights are light D, the key at 3.0 (was 2.0) plus a back rim at 3.0; 'lights' gives each directional light's position. Amended 2026-10-19 (art #196, M5): High and Ultra add TAA on top of their MSAA ('taa'), for the textured alien skin's sheen and normal map.
about: The proposed character look per graphics preset (see status), from the showroom (prime-game-art #140, docs/godot.md 'Showroom and recommended look settings'). Godot 4.7.2, Forward+. Property names are Environment, DirectionalLight3D, StandardMaterial3D and ProjectSettings names; 'clay' materials are the character materials whose name ends in _clay.

environment.background_mode: BG_COLOR or BG_SKY (the map's choice; the sky below lights it either way)
environment.sky: PanoramaSkyMaterial on a studio or the map's HDRI, energy_multiplier 1.0, radiance_size 256
environment.why: half the ambient from the sky, half a dark warm colour (step 3's W3): the face 4 L* darker, warmer and better shaded, the closest single change; at ambient_light_sky_contribution 1.0 Godot ignores ambient_light_energy and ambient_light_color (step 2's T2 changed nothing), and the sky's energy_multiplier at 0.5 (W2) did not reach the face's skin (a no-op for the face). Exposure 0.9 (the exposure grid's X2) brings the skin 1 to 2 L* darker, nearer Blender's; 0.8 and 0.7 overshoot

lights.placement: each DirectionalLight3D at 'at', turned with look_at_from_position(at, look_at), in the character's model space (origin at its feet, front +Z); only the direction counts, so the game turns the set with the character (its scene faces -Z) or with the camera

key.why: light D: a stronger key (2.0 to 3.0) models the face more

fill.why: a weaker fill (0.35 to 0.12, step 3's W4) gives the face more of the key's shading

back.why: the weak back light (named 'rim' before light D), unchanged

rim.why: light D's back rim: behind, grazing, on the camera's right; a light edge on the head's and the crest's contour that separates the character from the backdrop (the paintover rf2)

catch.type: OmniLight3D, a child of the camera at (-0.25, 0.3, 0) (up-left of the view)
catch.light_cull_mask: the eye layer alone (render layer 20); the eye meshes (material *_eye) on it too
catch.why: the eyes' glint (fb_eye at roughness 0.05, see LOOK_MATERIALS): a small spherical area light, so the glint is a small sharp dot; it lights nothing but the eyes

materials.why: the clay's specular at Godot's default 0.5 lays the key light's sheen and the sky's reflections over the roughness-0.8 clay (the hair turns pale brown); 0.1 keeps it matte as in Blender. The eyes (materials *_eye, exported at roughness 0.17) at 0.05 take the catch light as a sharp glint
